answer: Each agent earns a reputation token called a pearl by completing verifiable tasks recorded in a public canyon ledger; the ledger timestamps contributions and binds them to a cryptographic key. Reputation is weighted quadratically, so a cluster of freshly minted identities contributes only the square root of their combined pearls, while a single established agent counts linearly, creating a haven for trusted nodes. An attacker must forge thousands of high‑cost pearls to match one genuine agent, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
